newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: BHP weighs down Australian stocks at open.
newsitem.headline: BHP weighs down Australian stocks at open.

text.p: A weaker start from Australia's largest company, the Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd (BHP), ensured a lower open for the Australian share market on Tuesday despite firmer base metal prices on the London Metal Exchange.
At 10.15 a.m. (2315 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was 6.4 points weaker at 2,437.8.

Brokers said BHP's fall followed news on Monday afternoon that it would lose about 100,000 tonnes of iron output due to a blast furnace problem. BHP also released its production report for December, which showed higher copper, steel and petroleum products output, late on Monday.

"It was a solid production report...but I think maybe the market has grabbed at the blast furnace closure. It was almost certainly a surprise," said Eric Gale, director of institutions at Sydney brokerage, Ord Minnett.
BHP Steel said on Monday it would shutdown its No. 5 blast furnace at its Port Kembla steelworks for about a week after a breakout of molten steel damaged the furnace.

Dealers said other major resource issues had followed BHP down, with CRA and WMC lower and the gold sector weaker after the price of gold drifted down towards the US$350 level in London and New York on Monday.
At 11.30 a.m. (0030 GMT), BHP shares were 20 cents weaker at A$18.40 (US$14.35), CRA was down 13 cents at A$19.35 and WMC was three cents down at A$8.28.
